claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 22.95 km against a booked optimal of 16.7 km, an excess of 6.25 km. That excess is 37.43% of the optimal route, which clears the 20% establishment test, and 6.25 km clears the 0.8 km absolute test, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01. The governing figure is the trace distance, not the rounded 22.9 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The driver's traffic excuse cannot be run on this record. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02830-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, no validity window, and no shortest-lawful-alternative figure. POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-13 the driver's uncited assertion of a jam carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 181 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs fire. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on an unimpaired trace, and no independent corroboration is required.

The refund is arithmetic. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 16.7 + 0.28 x 22.5) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 23.4250. Charged_total is 30.18, so the refund is 30.18 - 23.4250 = 6.7550, rounded up to 6.80. That is 22.38% of charged_total, well below the 90% full-refund share, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, not from the trip record.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due on top of the distance refund. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero tolls and a zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route gantry and no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09. The POL-RD-02 figure already comprehends all pass-through lines and must not be added to.

The driver's profile does not support a repeat-deviation uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 395 is 0.0025, far below the 0.05 ratio test, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and the POL-RD-02 partial stands un-uplifted. I note the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is 0 but it is not the field POL-RD-06 names and I do not rely on it.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so the extra-corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08 for sub-30% excess claims is not engaged, and in any event the measured excess here is 37.43%, above 30%. The rider's other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and I cite none of them as a ground of decision.

The chat log is empty: zero messages, no first or last message timestamp. There is therefore no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no rider-caused detour under POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 either, since the trip record shows no amended pickup or dropoff and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. No distance is excluded before the POL-RD-01 test.

ruling.explanation:
The rider's claim and the platform's own trace agree, so this dispute is decided on the numbers.

(1) The deviation is ESTABLISHED. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02830 measures the trip between the recorded pickup and drop-off events at 22.95 km against the booked optimal of 16.7 km on EV-TRIP-02830 — an excess of 6.25 km, which is 37.43% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km). The trace distance governs; the rounded 22.9 km convenience copy on the trip record was not used for the threshold.

(2) The trace is not impaired. 181 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fires. No independent corroboration is required, and the POL-RD-08 burden shifts to the driver.

(3) The driver's traffic excuse does not answer the finding. You say there was a massive jam on the expressway. An external-traffic excuse is tested under POL-RD-03 against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02830-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): it names no road, carries no validity window and holds no shortest-lawful-alternative figure. POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13 read with POL-RD-08, the assertion carries no weight — it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because you named no evidence ID for an advisory, POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged (POL-RD-13(1)): this is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. The ruling records that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file.

(4) The arithmetic. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs; the surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 16.7 + 0.28 × 22.5) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 23.425. Charged_total is 30.18. Refund = 30.18 − 23.425 = 6.755, rounded UP to SGD 6.80. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share (22.38% of charged_total), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.80.

(5) No additions. There are no ERP gantries, no tolls and no airport surcharge on EV-FARE-02830, so POL-RD-09 corrects nothing and nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. No rider-requested detour or relocation rescues any part of the excess: the chat log EV-CHAT-02830 is empty (0 messages), no pickup or drop-off amendment is recorded (amended_optimal_distance_km is null), and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

(6) Driver conduct and profiles. The deviation is not MATERIAL (37.43% is below 50%; 6.25 km is below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 profile check is not required; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 395 (ratio 0.0025), so no repeat pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift follows and no driver-conduct referral arises. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the POL-RD-08 trigger of 4, so no extra corroboration is required. No profile field outside the ones POL-GEN-01 names is used as a ground of decision; the lifetime counters mentioned in the papers are context only.

(7) No escalation, and no referral. Confidence 0.95 is above the 0.70 floor. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, no timestamps conflict, no charge line is unmatched, and the trace is unimpaired. The monetary effect of SGD 6.80 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the ruling executes automatically on issue.

Confidence is 0.95. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-GPS-02830, EV-TRIP-02830 and EV-FARE-02830 — sits at weight 1.0. The 0.0-weight advisory EV-ADVIS-02830-01 is not relied on and does not enter the confidence cap; it is recorded only as an absence. The referrals list is empty because no clause produces one. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal it once within 30 days to the platform's help channel (POL-GEN-04).

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this is a route-deviation dispute on trip TRP-02830, and I find for the rider in part — a partial refund of SGD 6.80.

WHAT THE RECORDS SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02830) measures 22.95 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against a booked optimal route of 16.7 km (EV-TRIP-02830). The excess is 6.25 km, or 37.43% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 says the trace figure governs over the rounded 22.9 km convenience copy on the trip record, and on the trace figure both establishment tests pass — the excess is more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (which needs more than 50% or more than 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not required. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 181 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fire and no independent corroboration is needed. I accept both sides' claims on these points.

NOTHING REDUCES THE EXCESS. The chat log for this trip contains 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction that could excuse any part of the detour under POL-RD-04, and no waypoint to corroborate. Neither the pickup nor the drop-off was amended, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 16.7 km stands. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. Your statement, driver, that there was a massive jam and everyone was diverting, asserts an external traffic cause; no traffic advisory is on file for this trip — EV-ADVIS-02830-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no payload, so it can carry no fact. An uncited traffic assertion cannot be tested against an advisory, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 it does not reduce the measured excess or supply an adjusted optimal route. The assertion is therefore discarded and I record that no advisory was on file.

THE MONEY (POL-RD-02; the fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, EV-FARE-02830):
- charged_total: SGD 30.18
